questions.question: What happens when TurboFan-optimised code hits a value that breaks one of its speculative assumptions?
options: V8 deoptimises: it discards the optimised code and continues in a lower tier
V8 silently converts the value to match the assumption
The function is permanently blocked from running
questions.explanation: Optimised code is guarded by checks; when a guard fails V8 bails out (deoptimises) to a lower tier, which you can observe with --trace-deopt.

questions.question: Why do `{ x: 1, y: 2 }` and `{ y: 1, x: 2 }` end up with different hidden classes?
options: Because object literals never share hidden classes
Because hidden classes are built by property-addition order, so different orders follow different transition chains
Because y is alphabetically after x
questions.explanation: A hidden class (Map) records which properties were added and in what order; adding x then y and y then x produce different Maps.

questions.question: A property access site has seen objects of 12 different shapes. What is its inline cache state?
questions.explanation: One shape is monomorphic, a few (up to about 4 in V8) is polymorphic, and beyond that the site goes megamorphic and uses a slower generic lookup.

questions.question: Which habit best helps V8 keep objects on fast paths?
options: Initialise all properties in the constructor in a consistent order instead of adding or deleting them later
Use delete to remove properties you no longer need
Store numbers and strings in the same array to save memory
Create arrays with new Array(n) and fill them sparsely
questions.explanation: Consistent construction keeps objects on one shared hidden class; delete can push objects into dictionary mode, and mixed or holey arrays move to slower elements kinds.
